name: interface-optional
description: Every combination of address and MAC a Stairwell asset can report, because both are optional and the script used to treat either one as a reason to drop the host. `2001` has both. `2002` reports the `-` placeholder and `2003` an empty string -- Stairwell writes both for 'none reported' -- and each must arrive with its address and no MAC. `2004` has a MAC and no address. `2005` has neither, so it arrives as a hostname-only asset with no interface at all: an asset with no interface is a normal asset, and network_interface() answers None rather than an empty object precisely so the caller can leave the list empty. `2007` is the loopback case stated at the record level, which is the only level it can be stated at: the platform's NormalizeAddress drops 127.0.0.1 before it ever reaches an asset, so the `no_loopback_interfaces` invariant would pass whether or not the script filtered it. The script previously substituted 127.0.0.1 for every address-less record, and that is what `2006` catches -- no address, no MAC, no label, and therefore nothing to correlate on. With the synthetic in place it built a real interface, defeated the correlator check, and emitted an orphan asset that the `has_correlator` invariant fails on; with it gone the record is skipped and says so.

log_contains: stairwell: skipping asset 2006 with no address, MAC, or label
